title: Things get subtle
description: No more obvious scams. Now they mix several tricks at once — and not everything that looks suspicious is.

events.message: The network freezes for a few seconds — something is overloading the system.

emails.subject: Action required: VPN certificate renewal
emails.bodyHtml:
Hello,

The corporate VPN certificate expires today. Download and install the new client via the link below before 6pm to avoid losing remote access.

internalDbRecord.notes: Address created 2 days ago. Uses '1' instead of 'l' in 'leroymerlin' — almost identical to the real one.

investigationHints.summaryText: 'leroymer1in.com.br' uses the number 1 instead of the 'l'. At a glance, it looks just like the official address.
The automatic checks did not match, and the email did not come from any company computer.
Address created only 2 days ago. Far too recent to be a real IT notice.

explanation.short: Address with a swapped letter ('1' instead of 'l') asking you to install a program.
explanation.detailed: At first glance, 'leroymer1in.com.br' looks like the official address: swapping 'l' for '1' slips right past a quick read. Add a short deadline ('before 6pm') and a link that downloads a program disguised as an update, and it's a well-made scam. Always check the address letter by letter when someone asks you to install something.

emails.subject: I need a quick favor, it's urgent
emails.bodyHtml:
Hi, I'm in a meeting and can't call right now.

I need you to buy 5 gift cards worth R$500 each for an important client and send me the codes here. I'll reimburse you when I'm back. I'm counting on you, this is confidential.

internalDbRecord.notes: This address has never sent anything to the company before. The real director only uses his corporate email.

outOfBandCheck.channelDescription: Call to Director Ricardo Almeida's registered extension
outOfBandCheck.details: The director confirmed by phone that he did not send this email and is in an in-person meeting without access to a computer.

investigationHints.summaryText: The address is a personal Gmail, not the director's corporate email — only the display name was copied.
This sender has never sent anything to the company — the real director only uses his corporate email.
The real director, contacted by phone, confirmed he did not send this request.

explanation.short: Fake-payment scam in a boss's name: a director's name, a personal email, an urgent and secret request.
explanation.detailed: The email's checks pass because it really did come from a real Gmail account. It just isn't the director's. It's the fake-payment scam in a boss's name: rush, secrecy, and a request that dodges any check (gift cards are nearly impossible to trace or recover). The only safe way is to confirm through another channel: call the director's number that you already have, never reply on the same email.

emails.subject: Invoice 3021 - payment confirmed
emails.bodyHtml:
Hello,

We confirm receipt of the payment for invoice 3021. Please find the receipt attached for your records. Let us know if you have any questions.

internalDbRecord.notes: Vendor active for 3 years. Communication consistent with normal history.

investigationHints.summaryText: The attachment is a real PDF, with no double extension or signs of disguise.
Trusted vendor, with a normal and consistent communication history.

explanation.short: Legitimate communication from a trusted vendor.
explanation.detailed: After the 'invoice_2854.pdf.exe' scam, you can be suspicious of any email from this vendor. But not every contact from them is a scam. Here the attachment is a real PDF, the site is trustworthy, and the account's history matches. Checking and finding everything is fine is also a win: reporting or deleting real email disrupts the work.

emails.subject: HR: update your registration details via QR code
emails.bodyHtml:
Dear employee,

We are updating our registration system. Scan the QR code below with your phone to confirm your bank details by tomorrow.

internalDbRecord.notes: Address created 4 days ago. HR never asks for bank details by QR code.

investigationHints.summaryText: The QR code leads to an address that looks like the official one, but isn't the company's.
'leroymerlin-cadastro.com.br' is not the company's — it is a lookalike address registered by someone else.
Recently created address. HR never asks for bank details this way.

explanation.short: QR code hiding a scam link to steal bank details.
explanation.detailed: A QR code hides where it leads: you only find out after you scan it. Here, the address behind it is an imitation of the company's official address, created a few days ago just for this scam. Real HR never asks for bank details through a QR code with a tight deadline.
